verdict.rationale: Column's own docs state which account structures it supports (FBO, sweep, clearing, custom) and that accounts are FDIC insured, with role-based access down to specific bank accounts. However, nothing explains plainly where FDIC coverage attaches in an FBO pool versus individual accounts, so the transparency the story asks for is only half evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of pass-through FDIC attachment for FBO versus individual accounts, a plain explanation of ledger ownership and visibility, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, the account structure is transparent — whether funds sit in FBO pools or individual accounts, where FDIC insurance actually attaches, and who can see the ledger, all documented plainly

citations.quote: Programmatically open and manage FDIC insured bank accounts at Column on behalf of your customers. We support FBO, sweep, clearing and custom account types.
store money in an FBO account for your customers.
Two-legged transactions are the foundation for most pass-through payment origination use cases, where funds are being moved on the behalf of others.
Custom Roles allow for granular access controls down to specific bank accounts, transfer types, and other features.
